title: 10-day-old boy with vomiting
arrival: A 10-day-old boy is brought in by his mother. He was born without complications following a normal pregnancy. His mother reports that he vomited once earlier today but has otherwise been feeding well. He is alert and well appearing.

checkpoints.why: He is alert and well appearing.
No stridor, central cyanosis, or respiratory distress.
His pulse is strong, extremities are warm, and capillary refill is normal. His heart rate does not cross the high-risk threshold for his age band.
No convulsions, and no altered mental status with stiff neck or fever.
He is 10 days old, so the under-8-days criterion does not apply, and his temperature of 37.1°C is within range.
No swelling of the mouth, throat, or neck, and no wheezing.
He is feeding well, with no dehydration, ongoing diarrhoea, or severe pallor.
He is settled, not irritable or lethargic, and not in severe pain.
He is 10 days old, which falls within the 8-days-to-6-months band. Age alone meets yellow criteria.

keyCriterion: Yellow — Other: any infant 8 days to 6 months old (age alone)
feedbackWhy: He is 10 days old, which falls within the 8-days-to-6-months band. Age alone meets yellow criteria, even though he is well appearing and has no high-risk vital signs.
teachingPoint: He requires urgent evaluation and should be reassessed within two hours if he has not yet been evaluated in the treatment area.
